properties.description:
The bridge of option (c1) of dec:idea-reflow2s-own-design-moves-onto-flo2-io-or-stays-local: the design lives on flo2.io, and CI reads a copy committed per PR. tools/reflow2_design_copy.py mirrors flo2's ops/flo2-design-copy for the item layout.

- `hold`, before a PR's first design write: says whether this branch may write. It refuses while another branch holds the design, or while writes nobody holds are in flight (--adopt takes those into the PR deliberately).
- `copy`, last, after `git merge origin/main`: the same refusals, plus one until the branch contains main. It drops the hold claims, imports the rest with this repo's binary into a throwaway store, and exports the item layout into docs/design/reflow2/. Then it compares what it wrote with the source, and exits 2 naming any value the round trip changed (fact:bl-198).
- `status`: what is in flight, and who holds the design.

THE HOLD is a claim: `claim_region` on proj:reflow2, depth 0, note `design PR: <branch>`. IN FLIGHT is the live design without its hold claims, compared item by item with main's copy. After a merge nothing is in flight, so the hold is stale and there is no release step. --from reads a saved design instead of flo2.io; the tests and the break-glass path use it.

LIMIT: the guard binds whoever runs it. Claims are advisory, and the design records who wrote, not on which branch, so a session that writes without holding is not caught.



IN USE FROM 2026-10-10: the design moved onto flo2.io. The first real hold and copy was the PR that recorded the move (branch feat/reflow2s-design-moves-onto-flo2-io). Read through flo2.io's engine, status took 35 s on the whole design and found 0 items in flight against main's copy. .reflow2.toml (art:reflow2-design-pointer) names the hosted design.
properties.name: A design PR holds reflow2's hosted design before writing, and copies it into the repository last; the copy refuses another branch's work
